name: sol-audit
version: v2 at sol-audit commit 1a2ffb1c20d0d3aeb938a4d6086aa339e39175f7, guard-aware rules, published 2026-08-31

provenance.install: our own scanner, run from a local checkout of the v2 source
provenance.note: Superseded in the working tree by 3.0. Its rows stay because deleting a superseded run is not how this project corrects things.

run.tool_root_note: a git worktree of https://github.com/halobartku/sol-audit at 1a2ffb1, the commit whose message is `sol-audit v2: guard-aware rules. Real recall 0/11 -> 4/11`. v2 is not the working tree any more; v3 is, and v3 has its own declaration.
run.invocation_evidence: tools/emit_sol_audit.py, committed in this repository. v2 has no command line at all - it is a Python module, and the bench script committed alongside it emits per-class totals, not findings - so this adapter is the only thing that produces the shape raw/sol-audit.json holds: {"findings": [{rule_id, file, line}]}, with `file` the walked path. Its scanner.scan_text entry point exists at 1a2ffb1 and is the one this script calls. What this is NOT evidence for: the exact argv of the 2026-08-31 run, which nobody wrote down. It is evidence that the published file can be reproduced from a committed script and a pinned commit, which is a weaker claim, and it is the claim being made.
run.arg_defaults_note: the interpreter is a declared token because the corpus-1 checkout lives on a host whose only python is `python3`. The first attempt hard-coded `python`, all 35 invocations failed to launch, and the framework recorded 35 `unavailable` rather than 35 zeros. Pass --arg python=python3 there.

evidence.means: the number of .rs files the adapter opened AND carried through scanner.scan_text without an exception. A file the scanner threw on is not counted, because a crash is an outage and not a clean zero. v2 prints nothing of its own, so this line is the adapter speaking for it, and that is said here rather than implied.

positive_control.sample_source: the shape of raw/sol-audit.json, with one finding substituted for the fix site of the synthetic case

measurements.note: 4 / 11 real as published on 2026-08-31 with no per-run log. Re-run per case, per variant, through the framework on 2026-09-01 from the pinned v2 worktree. Still published while its corpus-2 twin is retired (KNOWN-LIMITATIONS 41), which is why it needed a log: a row on the front page that cannot show what it analysed is the defect the coverage gate exists to catch.

The weakest evidence on the clock: no run log, and 96 of 426 findings naming files that are not in the corpus. It is the only corpus-2 row that reports coverage_evidence `none`, and `python tools/run_all.py --verify-coverage` fails on it twice over: no run log, and every case it cannot resolve. Retired on the published pages on 2026-09-01 (docs/KNOWN-LIMITATIONS.md 41) in favour of v3, and marked retired rather than deleted, so it stays on the clock and stays countable. The run block above is how v2 can be driven now; this row was not produced by it and is retired rather than re-run.

retired.by: sol-audit v3, measured per case on all three profiles, 207 invocations
retired.reason: Superseded. This row has no run log on either corpus and 96 of its 426 findings name files the corpus rebuild removed. Re-running a superseded version of our own scanner would be work that flatters us and informs nobody.
